security_spec.violation_condition: OpenSBI (acting as RDSM in M-mode) writes to Smmtt/SmDAP domain protection CSRs (e.g., mttp or equivalent MTT registers) without a subsequent domain-aware fence (SFENCE.W.INVAL or SFENCE.VMA with domain operand), or the HSM suspend/resume path fails to save/restore domain protection CSR state, allowing a resumed hart to operate with stale or unvalidated domain isolation configuration.
security_spec.summary: OpenSBI as RDSM must synchronize Smmtt/SmDAP domain protection CSRs with proper domain-aware fences and preserve domain isolation state across HSM suspend/resume; missing fences after MTT CSR writes or stale CSR restore on resume can break supervisor domain isolation, allowing cross-domain privilege escape.

findings.finding: Domain context switch saves/restores sstatus, sie, stvec, sscratch, sepc, scause, stval, sip, satp, scounteren, senvcfg, srmcfg (lines 131-146) but has zero awareness of domain protection CSRs (mttp, mmte). No Smmtt/SmDAP CSR save/restore exists. If Smmtt were enabled, MTT configuration would leak between domains. SFENCE.W.INVAL (domain-aware fence) is also absent — only __sbi_sfence_vma_all() (line 140) follows SATP swap, which is insufficient for MTT cache invalidation.

The hart_context structure stores per-domain hart state (trap_ctx, sstatus, sie, stvec, sscratch, sepc, scause, stval, sip, satp, scounteren, senvcfg, srmcfg) but lacks fields for domain protection CSRs (mttp, mmte). Without these fields, domain-specific MTT root pointer and MTE configuration pointer cannot be saved/restored across domain context switches.

The sbi_hsm_data structure stores saved_mie, saved_mip, saved_medeleg, saved_mideleg, saved_menvcfg for non-retentive suspend/restore but has no fields for saved_mttp or saved_mmte. Without these fields, domain protection CSR state has nowhere to be persisted during suspend and cannot be restored on resume.

HSM non-retentive suspend save path saves MIE, MIP, MEDELEG, MIDELEG, MENVCFG (lines 427-432) but does NOT save any domain protection CSRs (mttp, mmte). During non-retentive suspend the hart loses power; all MTT configuration state is lost. Resume without save/restore would leave the hart with domain protection disabled (mttp=0 at hardware reset).

HSM non-retentive suspend restore path restores MENVCFG, MIDELEG, MEDELEG, MIE, MIP (lines 440-445) but does NOT restore mttp/mmte. After non-retentive suspend, hardware has lost all domain protection state. The restore path must write saved mttp/mmte values and execute SFENCE.W.INVAL. Without this, the resumed hart runs with domain protection disabled, breaking isolation guarantees before MRET to S-mode.

The warm resume path (entry for harts waking from non-retentive suspend) calls sbi_hsm_hart_resume_start() → sbi_hart_reinit() → sbi_hart_protection_configure() → sbi_hsm_hart_resume_finish(). sbi_hart_reinit() calls mstatus_init() which initializes mstatus, scounteren, mcounteren, menvcfg, mseccfg, mie, satp etc. but never touches mttp/mmte. sbi_hart_protection_configure() configures PMP-based isolation but is unaware of MTT-based domain protection. On hardware with Smmtt/SmDAP, mttp would remain at reset value (0=disabled).

mstatus_init() initializes mstatus, scounteren, mcounteren, mcountinhibit, mhpmevent, hstatus, mstateen0-3, sstateen0-3, menvcfg, mseccfg, mie, satp — but has no initialization of domain protection CSRs (mttp, mmte). Called by both cold boot (init_coldboot) and warm resume (init_warm_resume). In cold boot, MTT may carry stale entries from earlier firmware stages. In warm resume, MTT is at hardware reset default. mttp should be initialized (at minimum to 0=disabled) with a domain-aware fence.

sbi_hart_switch_mode() performs MRET to lower privilege after setting up mstatus, mepc, stvec/sscratch/sie/satp. Before MRET, if domain protection CSRs were modified, SFENCE.W.INVAL must be executed to ensure MTT configuration is visible to the hart's memory access checks. No such domain-aware fence exists. Used by sbi_hsm_hart_start_finish(), sbi_hsm_hart_resume_finish(), and switch_to_next_domain_context().

The M-mode trap handler has no handling for domain-protection-related traps (domain access faults that Smmtt/SmDAP would generate). Any such trap would fall through to the default case and be redirected to S-mode via sbi_trap_redirect(). S-mode has no way to distinguish a domain protection violation from a generic access fault. RDSM should intercept domain protection faults in M-mode to enforce domain isolation policy.

The HSM SBI ecall handler implements SBI_EXT_HSM_HART_START, STOP, GET_STATUS, SUSPEND but has no COVT/COVH domain protection SBI extension handlers. There is no SBI-level mechanism for S-mode to request domain ownership transitions that would require MTT reprogramming by M-mode RDSM.
